report.previous_run_delta: New/direct-fit: Cloudflare raised the Workers bundle ceiling to 64 MiB on Free and Paid plans, removing the former 3 MB compressed Free-plan constraint. Newly enforced/capability boundary: D1 Free now fails requests after its daily row limits, creating a spend-safe but availability-sensitive limit. Recovered/magnitude: Open Yap 1K makes 1,000 hours of full-duplex natural English conversation available on request for commercial and research use. Closed: MiniMax M3/M2.7 free routes passed their September 6 endpoint date. Detector failure: GMI SCALE Cohort 2 disclosed a $40K+ partner-credit surface, but the August 21 application deadline was missed; it is not presented as actionable.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED INFRASTRUCTURE DELTA; FREE-TIER CAPABILITY STRENGTHENING WITH ENFORCED DATABASE LIMIT
signals.changed: On September 4 Cloudflare replaced the former 3 MB compressed Workers Free bundle limit (10 MB Paid) with a 64 MiB uncompressed limit on every plan. Separately, from September 1 D1 Free queries fail after daily row-read or row-write limits are reached until 00:00 UTC.
signals.free_value: Workers Free can deploy bundles up to 64 MiB. D1 Free includes 5 million rows read/day, 100,000 rows written/day, 5 GB total storage, and no D1 egress charge.
signals.approximate_value: Not meaningfully priced as credits; it removes framework/dependency trimming and permits a more capable edge application at $0 while retaining hard usage stops.
signals.cash_required: $0 on Workers Free. The cited D1 limit behavior fails closed rather than generating usage charges.
signals.fit: Direct fit for the planned Cloudflare-based LEVERAGEdelta public projection; no startup-program qualification is required for the ordinary Free plan.
signals.catch: A larger bundle does not increase CPU or request quotas. D1 outages become possible at the daily account-wide caps, and full table scans consume row-read allowance quickly; indexes add write counts.
signals.window: The 64 MiB limit is live with no announced expiry. D1 enforcement is already active.
signals.immediate_exploit: Run wrangler deploy --outdir bundled/ --dry-run on LEVERAGEdelta, record Total Upload, then audit D1 queries for indexes and add a graceful cached/read-only state for limit errors. Stop after two hours.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED DATASET RELEASE; FULL CORPUS APPROVAL AND CUSTOM AGREEMENT REQUIRED
signals.changed: Open Yap 1K released September 3 with 1,000 hours across 1,602 dual-channel natural English conversations, recorded at 48 kHz and available free on request for commercial and research use.
signals.free_value: An immediate 8.9-hour CC-BY-4.0 sample plus, after review and a recipient-specific agreement, the 1,000-hour corpus with separate speaker tracks, shared timing, word-level machine transcripts, and audio/device metadata.
signals.approximate_value: Unpriced but plausibly substantial labor/data replacement: the publisher positions it as the largest commercially usable natural two-speaker English corpus and roughly 3.5 times the next-largest comparable wideband corpus.
signals.cash_required: $0 dataset license and access fee. Storage, transfer into the recipient S3 bucket, preprocessing, and model training compute are not free.
signals.fit: Individuals or companies may request access by identifying themselves and describing the intended use; no funding, incorporation, team-size, or revenue gate is stated.
signals.catch: The full corpus is not open-download CC-BY; it uses a separate data-use agreement and approval. Redistribution, speaker identification, and identifiable voice cloning are prohibited. Transcripts are machine-generated and not human-verified; the sample is hand-picked, and training 1,000 hours is compute-intensive.
signals.window: No application deadline or expiry is published.
signals.immediate_exploit: Do not download the full corpus speculatively. Inspect the 8.9-hour sample against one existing interruption, diarization, or voice-agent evaluation need; request the full set only if a concrete experiment passes.

program_surface_results: GMI Cloud SCALE Cohort 2 is a confirmed equity-free six-week program advertising $500 MaaS credit on acceptance, 1:1 matching up to $4,500, and up to $40,000 in partner credits. Its published application deadline was August 21 and cohort announcement date September 7, so it is closed rather than actionable.
The GMI page also displays a $125,000 MaaS/compute figure without enough context to treat it as a per-startup entitlement; it was excluded from valuation.

This is a Golden Signal detector failure: the application-only partner-benefit page should have been escalated before August 21. Future scans must search upcoming cohort calendars and partner-benefit pages before cohort-announcement dates, not only at launch or announcement.
